title: In 459 IBL mouse sessions, 5-11 Hz rhythmic spiking formed a lick-locked orofacial system and a septo-hippocampal system; mesoscale septal input did not predict the regional map
abstract: Question: the medial septum (MS) paces hippocampal theta. Does anatomical input from the septal pacemaker tell which mouse brain regions contain 5-11 Hz rhythmic neurons? Data: IBL Brain-Wide Map 2026 Q2 autocorrelograms of 75,129 good units (459 sessions); Knox 2019 connectome model; 14 Allen tracer experiments with MS or NDB injections (post hoc); lick times and spike windows of 16 IBL probes. Method: a damped-cosine fit to each autocorrelogram gives a rhythm z value (rhythmic if z >= 5); regional shares in 200 structures; plan hashed before structure statistics; 1,000 Gaussian-process spatial surrogate maps. Results: 16.1% of units were rhythmic at 5-11 Hz (0.6% at 12-20 Hz). The regional map was reliable (split-half rho 0.52) and had two clusters with the same 6.75 Hz median frequency: septo-hippocampal (TRS 0.63, MS 0.58, LSc 0.51, DG 0.43, CA1 0.40) and orofacial (SPVC 0.51, SSp-m 0.49, IRN 0.42, V 0.41). Planned test H1 failed: Knox MS+NDB input did not predict the share (Spearman 0.05, spatial p 0.36; 64th percentile of 291 sources), and no source passed the null. Allen tracer data placed MS output in septum and hippocampal formation; the 20 strongest MS targets had twice the share of other regions (0.28 vs 0.135, p 0.001, exploratory), but across all regions the tracer predictor also failed (rho 0.06, p 0.33). Licks separated the systems: 94% of rhythmic orofacial units were locked to the 6-8 Hz lick cycle, 2% of septo-hippocampal units, and 42% of rhythmic units in other regions. The planned amplitude contrast (rhythm inside minus outside lick bouts, orofacial minus septo-hippocampal) was not resolved (0.30, 95% CI -0.14 to 0.77). Limitations: whole-session autocorrelograms, behaviour checked in 16 probes only, cluster lists defined after seeing the map, one task in head-fixed mice, no whisking or breathing signals.

display.caption: A: share of good units with 5-11 Hz autocorrelogram rhythm (z >= 5) in the 60 highest of 200 mouse brain regions (IBL Brain-Wide Map 2026 Q2). Blue: septo-hippocampal regions; orange: orofacial and lick regions; grey: other. Bars show binomial SE; dashed line: share over all units. B-D: example autocorrelograms (normalised to their 1-1.94 s asymptote) of a rhythmic and a non-rhythmic unit in CA1, SSp-m and VISp. Grey lines mark multiples of 1/7 Hz.

A: planned test H1. Knox 2019 model input from MS+NDB against the regional rhythmic share (Spearman 0.05, Gaussian-process spatial surrogate p 0.36). B: post hoc check with 7 Allen MS tracer experiments (rho 0.06, p 0.33). Strong septal targets are rhythmic, but many rhythmic orofacial regions get no septal input. C: Spearman rho of each of 291 Knox sources with the map; MS+NDB is at the 64th percentile and no source passes the 95% spatial-null point.

Behaviour check in 16 IBL probes. A: probe-median rhythm amplitude outside (>1 s from a lick) and inside lick bouts; rhythm grows inside bouts in both systems. B: vector strength of spikes in the lick cycle for rhythmic septo-hippocampal (n=312) and orofacial (n=236) units. C: share of rhythmic units locked to licks (Rayleigh p < 1e-6 and vector strength >= 0.1), probe mean with 95% probe-bootstrap interval: 0.02, 0.94 and 0.42.
